annotations.title: Publish, approve or archive a page

description: Move a page through its lifecycle by naming the target `state`: "published" makes the newest version the one readers see, and puts it into search and recall (refused where the wiki requires an approval - ask for one instead); "awaiting_approval" asks for one, optionally directed at a `reviewer`; "approved" approves AND publishes in the same act; "changes_requested" sends it back to the author with a `note` saying why (required); "draft" withdraws an approval request, or unpublishes a live page - readers lose it; "discarded" drops unpublished changes and goes back to what is live, keeping the discarded version in the history; "archived" archives the page AND everything beneath it, removing the lot from the tree, search and every reader path while its paths keep redirecting; "restored" brings an archived subtree back. The response says how many pages the act covered - more than one for an archive or a restore.

note.description: note is required when requesting changes.

page.description: page is the page's id or its full path within the wiki.

reviewer.description: reviewer optionally directs an approval request at one person (a user id).

space.description:
space optionally selects which of your spaces to act in (an id or name
 from list_spaces). Omit it when you belong to a single space.

state.description:
state is the target:
   "published"          - publish the newest version. Where the wiki requires
                          an approval this is refused: ask for one instead.
   "awaiting_approval"  - ask for an approval. Optionally name a `reviewer`.
   "approved"           - approve AND publish in one act.
   "changes_requested"  - send it back to draft with a `note` saying why.
   "draft"              - withdraw an approval request, or unpublish a live
                          page (readers lose it).
   "discarded"          - drop unpublished changes and go back to what is
                          live. The discarded version stays in the history.
   "archived"           - archive the page AND everything beneath it. It
                          leaves the tree, search and every reader path; its
                          paths keep redirecting.
   "restored"           - bring an archived page and its subtree back.

wiki.description: wiki is the wiki the page is in - its id or slug.
